Flexible record parsing and demultiplexing to FASTX/SAM/BAM/CRAM.

This tool reads multiple FASTX/SAM/BAM/CRAM inputs, identifies and extracts
technical sequences (barcodes, UMIs, adapters) with error tolerance using an
approximate matcher, writes FASTX/SAM/BAM/CRAM data with preserved
per-record segment qualities, fanning a record pool out into per-sample, and
optionally per-sample and per-library, files. And, in a single pass!

MENTAL MODEL

 1. Scan the inputs and match each tag --group(s) against each record
 2. Pull those matched bases into named --extract streams
 3. Route the record: assign to a --sample, else unassigned, or --remove it
 4. Set streams as the primary record sequences with --template
 5. Also set streams into SAM tags with --tag(s)
 6. Write records by fanning them to files by sample, sub-sample, ordinal

A "pool" is all input records for one run of unmux.

EXAMPLES

 1. Simply convert FASTQ to uBAM:

  unmux in.fq --out out.bam

 2. Extract a slice of each input record into a new FASTQ:

  unmux in.fq --extract myslice=0:0:9 --template myslice > out.fq

 3. Demux a library where the barcodes can be anywhere into per-sample BAMs:

  unmux r1.fq r2.fq --group bc=bc.tsv --sample s=bc::t01 --out %sample.bam

 4. Split a multi-read-group BAM into per-sample BAMs by its @RG header:

  unmux in.bam --group rg=@RG::SM --sample-from-group rg --out %sample.bam

Notation (also see param docs below with expressive examples):

  file:start:end   0-based, half-open; end is the record LENGTH;
                   negative counts from the record END. The FIRST number
                   is the input file index. 1:5:9 = file 1 & bases [5,9).
  @grp             a group's matched span. @grp+off:len & @grp-off:len
                   step past & before it (trailing number is a LENGTH!),
                   in the matched tag's orientation (see bothStrands).
  @grpA..@grpB     the region between two matched spans.
  @grp::COLUMN     the matched tag's value in a tag-file column, or its id.
  @RG[::F[::F]]    an input read-group --group source (SAM/BAM/CRAM only);
                   bare = by RG ID, or by subfield(s), e.g. @RG::SM::LB.
  +                concat streams (cb+umi) or 'AND' samples (gA::a+gB::b).
  |                fall back to the next stream when one is absent (--tag only).
  ~                reverse-complement the stream (~cb, BC=~bc).
  ,                list separator ('OR' a tag pool & attribute lists).
  %XX              percent-escape a byte in a tag sep/qual-sep value, a
                   COLUMN, or an output path (%20=space, %2C=comma).
  %pool            the pool ID (see --pool).
  %sample          the sample ID (--out only)
  %sample::COLUMN  the routing sheet row's value in COLUMN (--extract only).
  %sub_sample      the sub-sample ID (@RG LB) (--out only).
  %ordinal         1-based read ordinal (R%ordinal → R1, R2) (--out only).
  %source          0-based input file idx (--unassigned or --remove only).

Usage: unmux [READS]... [OPTIONS]

Arguments:
  [READS]...
          Input files, positional (FASTX/SAM/BAM/CRAM; auto-detected).
          
          0-based by order, the first file is index 0 (splitcode-style). With no
          inputs at all, file 0 defaults to stdin, so bare unmux reads stdin.
          Mutually exclusive with --in. Inputs must agree on yes/no qualities
          FASTA cannot blend with a quality-containing FASTQ/SAM/BAM/CRAM.
          SAM tags in a FASTX record-name comment are lifted onto the record,
          and a malformed one stops the run.
          
            unmux r1.fq r2.fq i1.fq   files 0, 1, 2
            unmux < reads.fq          file 0 from stdin (no args = stdin)

Options:
      --in <N=PATH>
          Input files set with N=PATH for explicit 0-based file indices.
          
          Repeatable; indices must be unique and contiguous from 0 (flag order
          is free; a gap or non-zero start is an error). PATH may be '-' for
          stdin (at most once). Mutually exclusive with positional inputs.
          
            --in 0=r1.fq.gz --in 1=r2.fq.gz   file 0 = r1, file 1 = r2
            --in 0=- --in 1=r2.fq.gz          file 0 from stdin, file 1 = r2
          
          [default: /dev/stdin]

      --pool <ID>
          Identifier for the input pool; fills the placeholder %pool.
          
          Optional, and defaults to the common stem of the input filenames.
          SAM/BAM/CRAM output needs it to be printable ASCII.
          
            --pool lib01   the %pool placeholder is now set to 'lib01'

      --out <PATTERN>
          Output path for demultiplexed records.
          
          Format set by extension (FASTX/SAM/BAM/CRAM). '-' or /dev/stdout
          writes standard output in the input format. Read groups and SAM tags
          are SAM/BAM/CRAM-only; FASTX puts --tag values in the record-name
          comment. BAM stores a U base as T. Missing parent dirs are created.
          Placeholders fan-out the pool into multiple files including %pool,
          %sample, %sub_sample, and %ordinal. Outputs that would be one
          file are refused: paths differing only in case (one file on a
          case-insensitive file system), two spellings of one file, a metrics
          file on another output's path, an --unassigned or --remove path
          equal to an --out path only once placeholders expand, or an output
          that is a file the run reads under any name (an input, a tag file,
          the sample sheet, or the reference and its indexes). Pass the --out
          pattern itself to --unassigned or --remove to keep those records
          in the --out file.
          
            --out out.bam                   one file with all assigned records
            --out %sample.bam               one file per sample
            --out %sample.%sub_sample.bam   per sample and sub-sample
            --out %pool.R%ordinal.fq.gz     per pool, per template ordinal
          
          [default: /dev/stdout]

      --group <SPEC>
          Tag-group definition or attributes (repeatable; accumulates).
          
          NAME=SOURCE is the UMI/barcode/adapter set; NAME::ATTRS constrains
          matching. Tags may use IUPAC codes, and a U in a read or a tag matches
          as T. A matched @grp span is error-corrected by default. Each tag in a
          set needs its own ID; pool several tags into one sample with
          --sample NAME=GROUP::ID1,ID2.
          
          A set is refused when one read can match two of its tags at one place
          within dist, counting a shorter tag inside a longer one and, with
          bothStrands=true, the reverse strand. With mode=nearest, which
          leaves such reads unassigned, this is only a warning unless the read
          matches both tags exactly. Pairs that one read can match only through
          an indel are refused only when no mode is set: add mode=nearest
          (recommended) or mode=all, which keeps assigning such reads by
          tie-break, to run with warnings that list them. Long tags too costly
          to compare under a large indel budget count as such pairs, and so are
          refused when no mode is set. Matches cut short by partial5 or
          partial3 are not checked. Without anchor, tags slide along a whole
          record or any window wider than they are, and two of them can then
          both match one read at shifted positions, as ACGTAC and CGTACG
          both match TACGTACGT, which the check does not flag.
          
          Sources (NAME::SOURCE):
          
            bc=tags.tsv        from a TSV file with id and seq columns; any
                               other column can feed a @bc::COLUMN extract
            bc={AAC,ACG,TTG}   inline set, auto tag IDs
            bc={a=AAC,b=ACG}   inline set, explicit tag IDs
            rg=@RG             the input @RG read groups, keyed by RG ID
            rg=@RG::SM         ...keyed by a subfield (SM here; also LB)
            rg=@RG::SM::LB     ...two tiers: SM then LB (sample, sub_sample)
          
          Attributes (NAME::key=val):
          
            bc::loc=1:0:8            file 1 bases [0,8) (default: whole record)
            bc::dist=1               allow 1 substitution (default: 0)
            bc::dist=1:1:2           1 sub + 1 indel, total ≤ 2
            bc::mode=nearest         keep best only if it beats runner-up...
            bc::delta=2              ...by ≥ 2 (default: 1; needs mode=nearest)
            bc::next=bc3:0-4         bc3 follows, 0-4 bp past this match
            bc::prev=bc1             require bc1 to have matched earlier
            bc::minFindsPerGroup=1   group matches ≥ once (keeplist)
            bc::maxFindsPerGroup=1   group matches ≤ once
            bc::minFindsPerTag=1     per-tag bounds (also use maxFindsPerTag)
            bc::findOne              exactly one match (unambiguous single tag)
            bc::bothStrands=true     match forward and reverse-complement
            bc::partial5=3           5' truncation ok but ≥3 bp must match
            bc::partial3=3:0.1       same at the 3'-end, and ≤10% mismatches
            bc::anchor=5p            anchor tags' 5-prime base at loc.start
            bc::anchor=3p            anchor tags' 3-prime base at loc.end
            bc::match=i7+i5          match tags on joined --extract streams
          
          A reverse-strand match (bothStrands=true) is read in its tag's own
          orientation, as if the record were reverse-complemented: @grp
          streams from it are reverse-complemented with their qualities
          reversed, and offsets and next=G:lo-hi windows step from it in that
          orientation (+ toward the record start). A windowed next= target
          matches on that match's strand (or either strand, with its own
          bothStrands=true); a bare next=G target keeps its own loc and
          strands. The match itself is still chosen in read coordinates, so
          where the tag matches the same bases in a record and its reverse
          complement, the two give the same spans and windowed targets.
          
          A match= group joins an @grp self-span error-corrected, as a
          --tag without raw=true writes it, and any other stream, such as
          1:0:8 or @grp+0:8, as the observed bases. A self-span whose tag
          has an ambiguity code, such as N, also joins as the observed bases.
          
          When dist allows an edit, a loc, next or match= window wider than a
          tag lets a read match another tag at a shifted position as closely
          as its true tag: the leftmost match then wins, or with mode=nearest
          the read is left unmatched. Unmux warns where it estimates this for
          over 0.3% of reads with an error, suggesting mode=nearest, a window
          as wide as the tags if no indel upstream shifts the barcode, or, with
          an indel budget, a window wider than the tags by twice that budget. A
          whole-record search, or a window that runs to the record end, has the
          same risk but is not warned about.
          
          An @RG source reads the input header's read groups instead of
          matching sequences (SAM/BAM/CRAM only; no barcode attributes, no
          @-span). Pair with --sample-from-group to write one file per
          read group, sample, or library.
          
          An aligned input (@SQ present) split into SAM/BAM keeps every
          record whole, secondary and supplementary included: flags, position,
          CIGAR, MAPQ, mate fields, and tags. Each file gets the input @HD,
          @SQ, @PG, and @CO lines, only its own @RG lines, and an unmux
          @PG; records keep input order. --rg-tag has no effect there, and
          --template, --tag, sequence-matching groups, aligned CRAM output,
          FASTX outputs beside SAM/BAM ones, and several inputs are errors.
          For unmapped records, run samtools reset on the outputs.

      --extract <SPEC>
          Make a named record segment into a stream NAME=[SPEC] (repeatable).
          
          NAME becomes a stream for --template, --tag, and group match=. An
          extracted stream carries both bases AND qualities.
          
          file:start:end is 0-based half-open; the trailing number is an END
          (full record length); negatives count from the record end. The
          anchored @grp forms take a LENGTH as the trailing number instead.
          
          The @grpA..@grpB form is the bases from the end of grpA's match to
          the start of grpB's, in grpA's orientation. It is empty, but still
          present, where a group is unmatched or grpB does not follow grpA in
          the same input file.
          
          A @grp form anchored on a reverse-strand match (bothStrands=true)
          is taken in the tag's orientation: @grp+off:len steps toward the
          record start, and the bases are reverse-complemented and the qualities
          reversed, so the stream reads as the tag does.
          
          The @grp::COLUMN form is the matched tag's text in a column of the
          group's tag file, where a blank means the tag's seq. Header case is
          ignored unless two headers differ only by case, and a header character
          other than letters, digits, '_', '-', and '.' is percent-escaped.
          Values may hold printable ASCII and spaces. The tag ID is @grp::id,
          also for an inline set, and @grp::seq is the same as @grp. Column
          streams have no qualities, so only --tag takes them, and a tag built
          from one has no quality tag. A match= group has columns but no span.
          
          The %sample::COLUMN form is the text in a --sample-sheet column of
          the row that routed the record, so rows of one sample may differ, e.g.
          nuc=%sample::same_cell. Where that cell is blank, every tag built
          from the stream is left out. sample and sub_sample work with any
          sample flag, e.g. sm=%sample::sample. Headers and values follow the
          @grp::COLUMN rules.
          
            r=0:9:end          file 0, base 9 to the end
            bc=1:0:8           file 1, bases [0,8)
            tail=0:-10:end     last 10 bases of file 0
            mid=0:5:-2         file 0, base 5 to (length - 2)
            cb=@grp            the group's own matched span
            umi=@grp+19:9      9 bases, 19 past grp's match end
            up=@grp-0:9        9 bases just left of grp's match
            ins=@grpA..@grpB   region between two anchors
            cell=@grp::cell    the matched tag's value in the cell column
            t=@grp::a%20b      the same for a column headed 'a b'
            name=@grp::id      the matched tag's ID

      --template <SPEC>...
          Set which streams become the primary record sequences (repeatable).
          
          Each name is an --extract stream (an input record is not a stream
          until extracted). Concatenate with '+'; one value per output record
          (R1, R2, ...). Optional; with none the full input is the raw output.
          
          SAM/BAM/CRAM allows at most two ordinals; multi-FASTX may have more.
          ::raw=true emits observed bases for a stream from a corrected @grp
          (default: corrected; no effect on a never-corrected stream). On a
          reverse-strand match, observed bases are in the tag's orientation, as
          the corrected ones are; the obs of --qc-tag stays in the read's.
          
          A record keeps the input tags of the read its first bases come from.
          Per-base tags such as OQ follow its bases: a trimmed, reordered, or
          flipped record takes the matching slices, reversed where flipped
          (bases, as in E2, reverse-complemented). A stream from a
          reverse-strand match counts as flipped unless ~ turns it back.
          Others, such as MM/ML, stay only on a record that copies that
          whole read in order; otherwise they are left out, with a warning, as
          are all per-base tags of a record that joins reads or holds a
          corrected barcode.
          
            --template cdna               one record = the whole cdna stream
            --template cb+umi             concatenate two streams into one
            --template r1 r2              two output records (a pair)
            --template r1 --template r2   same, repeated-flag form
            --template cb::raw=true       observed bases of a corrected stream
            --template ~r1                reverse-complement the stream

      --tag <SPEC>
          SAM tag binding or attributes (repeatable; accumulates).
          
          TAG=STREAM[+STREAM] concats record bases (join with '+'); TAG::ATTRS
          sets qual/sep/raw. A multi-stream tag joins sequences with sep
          (default: '-') and qualities with qual-sep (default: a space).
          Default qual tags pre-exist for: CB/CY CR/CY RX/QX BC/QT OX/BZ.
          
          A tag that two writers would set is an error. The writers are each
          binding, its qual tag (named or default), and --qc-tag; where a
          default qual tag clashes, set qual=none or qual=TAG. The exception
          is CB and CR, which may both default to CY: a record's CY holds
          the CR qualities where CR writes them (the SAM spec pairs them) and
          the CB qualities elsewhere. The tag RG is reserved for the read
          group, which unmux sets itself on SAM/BAM/CRAM output.
          
          A stream may list others after '|' to use, in order, when it is
          absent, and '|' binds tighter than '+'. A tag is written only when
          every stream in it, or one of its fallbacks, is present; otherwise the
          tag, its quality tag, and any input copies of them are left out.
          
          A tag built from an @grp::COLUMN or %sample::COLUMN stream, or a
          record's tag that falls back to one, has no quality tag, since
          qualities could not line up with its text: the default one is left out
          (a carried one is dropped). Setting qual=TAG is an error unless each
          part of the tag has a choice with bases. Such a stream cannot take ~,
          and raw does not change it.
          
            --tag RX=umi             UMI tag (auto quality tag QX)
            --tag CB=bc1+bc2+bc3     join three barcode streams
            --tag xc=cell+bc2+bc3    join column text and barcode streams
            --tag CB=cell|bc1+bc2    column text if the row has it, else bc1
            --tag CB::sep=_          join sequences with '_' not '-'
            --tag CB::qual=CY        name the paired quality tag
            --tag CB::qual=none      emit no quality tag
            --tag CB::qual-sep=%20   join qualities with a space
            --tag CR=bc::raw=true    set the observed (uncorrected) bases
            --tag BC=~bc             reverse-complement the stream

      --rg-tag <K=V>...
          Shared @RG header fields for every output read group (repeatable).
          
            --rg-tag PL=ILLUMINA CN=Acme   sequencing platform and center
            --rg-tag PU=run1.lane1         platform unit

      --qc-tag [<TAG>]
          Per-record QC in a UTF-8 JSON tag value for how the record was routed.
          
          Bare --qc-tag uses tag ZS; --qc-tag=TAG names another 2-char tag which
          must start with X/Y/Z or contain a lowercase char. QC is available for
          assigned, unassigned, and removed records.
          
            ...           no --qc-tag means no QC is written
            --qc-tag      JSON in tag ZS (the default)
            --qc-tag=ZQ   JSON in tag ZQ

      --sample <SPEC>
          Sample fan-out target SAMPLE[::SUB_SAMPLE]=SELECTOR (repeatable).
          
          SELECTOR is group::id-or-seq[,...] (comma is OR pool), a bare group
          (any of its tags), or several joined with '+' (AND across groups).
          SAMPLE → @RG SM and SUB_SAMPLE → @RG LB.
          
          A read goes to the first sample whose selector it satisfies. Two
          samples claiming one tag combination are an error, and selectors over
          different groups that one read can both satisfy, as s1=i7::a and
          s2=i5::b can, are warned about.
          
          Exclusive with --sample-sheet and --sample-from-group.
          
            --sample s1=bc::t01          route tag t01 to sample s1
            --sample s1=bc::t01,t02      OR pool: any listed tag
            --sample s1=i7::a+i5::b      AND: needs both indices
            --sample s1::lib9=bc::t01    sub_sample lib9 (→ @RG LB)
            --sample s1::%pool=bc::t01   sub_sample from pool ID

      --sample-sheet <FILE>
          Input sample sheet in TSV format (the table form of --sample).
          
          A required sample column (→ @RG SM), an optional sub_sample
          column (→ @RG LB), then one column per group. A group cell holds a
          tag ID or sequence; sample/sub_sample cells are plain labels. Rows
          sharing a sample are OR'd into one pool; group columns filled in the
          same row are AND'd (a match is needed in each). Below, s1 needs i7 a
          AND i5 b; s2 pools (i7 c AND i5 d) OR (i7 e AND i5 f).
          
          A read goes to the first row it satisfies. Rows of two samples that
          one read can both satisfy, as rows filling different group columns
          can, are warned about.
          
          Every other column must be a group or be read by a %sample::COLUMN
          extract; skip extra metadata columns with --sample-sheet-ignore.
          Exclusive with --sample and --sample-from-group.
          
            --sample-sheet samples.tsv
          
          Example:
          
            sample  sub_sample  i7  i5
            s1      lib9        a   b
            s2                  c   d
            s2                  e   f

      --sample-sheet-ignore <COLUMN>
          A --sample-sheet column to skip unread (repeatable).
          
          For per-sample metadata unmux does not use. The ignored column's cells
          may hold any value. It must be in the sheet's header and may not be
          sample, sub_sample, or a declared group. Requires --sample-sheet.
          
            --sample-sheet-ignore assay   skip the assay column
            --sample-sheet-ignore notes   repeat the flag to skip more

      --sample-from-group <GROUP>
          Make every tag in GROUP its own sample, 1-to-1 (a shortcut).
          
          The "just split by barcode" mode: each tag in GROUP becomes a sample
          with no --sample lines and no sheet to maintain. Each sample's ID
          (@RG SM, and thus %sample in --out) is the tag's ID: the id
          column when the tag file names it, else the sequence itself for an
          inline tag written without id=. An optional sub_sample column in the
          group's tag file sets @RG LB. Records whose GROUP tag matches
          nothing are unassigned, as with --sample.
          
          Exclusive with --sample and --sample-sheet.
          
            --sample-from-group bc   one sample per tag in group bc
            --sample-from-group rg   one sample per tag; rg may be an @RG group
          
          With --out %sample.bam the files are named by that tag ID:
          
            named tags (id column)    s01.bam, s02.bam, ...
            inline tags with no id=   ACGT.bam, TGCA.bam, ...

      --unassigned <PATTERN>
          Output path pattern for records matching no sample.
          
          The only placeholders are %pool and %source (input file index);
          %source fans these to one file per input record. Without this flag,
          unassigned records are dropped. Unmux warns when unassigned fraction
          reaches ≥20% of the pool. Given the --out pattern itself, these
          records share the --out file, whose SAM/BAM/CRAM header then also
          declares the pool read group; a run where a sample there has the
          pool's read group ID is refused.
          
            --unassigned unmatched.%source.fq.gz   one file per input file
            --unassigned unmatched.fa              all segments in one FASTA

      --remove <SEL[=PATH_PATTERN]>
          Records to remove via SEL[=PATH_PATTERN] (repeatable).
          
          A record matching SEL (a group or group::id) is removed and tallied as
          removed (distinct from --unassigned). With =PATH_PATTERN the removed
          records are written to the output path otherwise they are simply
          ignored. SEL is required. The only placeholders allowed in
          PATH_PATTERN are %pool and %source (input file index). Given
          the --out pattern itself, removed records share the --out file,
          with the read group rules of --unassigned.
          
            --remove phiX                      drop records matching phiX group
            --remove bc::t99                   drop one specific tag's records
            --remove phiX=phiX.%source.fq.gz   ...and write them out

      --metrics-per-sample <PATTERN>
          Per-sample metrics TSV with one data row per fan-out target.
          
          Only %pool is a valid path placeholder.
          
            --metrics-per-sample %pool.unmux.per_sample.tsv

      --metrics-summary <PATTERN>
          Pool-level summary metrics TSV.
          
          Only %pool is a valid path placeholder.
          
            --metrics-summary %pool.unmux.summary.tsv

      --metrics-unassigned <PATTERN>
          Unassigned-reason metrics TSV with one row per reason seen.
          
          Only %pool is a valid path placeholder.
          
            --metrics-unassigned %pool.unmux.unassigned.tsv

      --require-samples-explain-all-tags
          Fail fast unless every tag of every group named by a --sample and
          --sample-sheet selector is claimed by some sample (no tag in
          a sampled group left unclaimed). Off by default; applies only when
          samples are declared.

      --per-record
          Disable auto pair-detection. Treat each record as single-end, even
          when one input looks interleaved (mate-name pairing) or holds paired
          SAM/BAM/CRAM records (flag 0x1). Both are otherwise auto-detected,
          and SAM/BAM/CRAM mates must be adjacent and are ordered by their flags
          (except in an aligned read-group split, which keeps records whole).
          With several inputs, where a read takes one record from each, an input
          holding both mates of a pair is refused, as they would be split.

      --reference <FASTA>
          Indexed FASTA (with a .fai) to read a reference-compressed CRAM.
          
          Records decode as samtools decodes them, including the MD and NM
          tags the CRAM left out for the reference to restore.
          Before any output is written, every CRAM @SQ contig must be in the
          FASTA (matched by SN) with the same LN and, where @SQ has
          one, the same M5. Other @SQ fields such as UR are not used.
          SAM/BAM/FASTX inputs ignore it, and a run with no CRAM input warns
          that it is unused.
          
            --reference ref.fa   decode CRAM input against ref.fa

      --skip-reference-check
          Skip the --reference check against CRAM @SQ lines.
          
          For a CRAM whose header lists contigs the FASTA lacks and no record
          uses. A record on a missing contig still fails as it is decoded.

      --compression <LEVEL>
          Compression level 0-9 for BGZF (BAM) and gzip (FASTX.gz).
          CRAM uses its own codecs and ignores this.
          
          [default: 5]

      --threads <THREADS>
          Worker thread count.
          
          More threads speed up large inputs; 1 runs fully serially.
          
          [default: 8]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version
